notes: How this part was researched: the session's shared web-search allowance ran out after this part's first thirteen searches (five of the six legislative candidates). Everything else was read directly, one request at a time: each county's, city's and school district's own site, the Minnesota DFL's list of endorsed candidates and local party units' sites, the Legislative Reference Library, Wikipedia, the campaign websites the candidates filed with the Secretary of State, campaign addresses that official, party or news pages link to, and two local news sites' own election pages (Eden Prairie Local News, CCX Media). No search engine was read in place of the search tool. Likely campaign and party-unit addresses were also tried by asking only whether the name has an address on the network; three campaign sites were first found that way and then read (bendavismn.com, leeforowatonna.com, judgekevinross.com).

The campaign websites the candidates filed were learned by running the kit's own step (python -m ballot.local_sites files) on a scratch copy of the database; the real database was only read. Ten of the thirty filed one, and each was opened and read before it was listed here: Kupec, Marty, Ajouri, Schuette, Sencer-Mura, Narverud, Groff, Bielefeldt, Salway and Ross. Four more were found and read: Ben Davis's (the 8th Congressional District Republicans' 2026 Candidates page links it for HD 6A), Alejandro Caceres Aranda's (CCX Media's candidate page and the Senate District 43 DFL link it), Aaron Casper's (Eden Prairie Local News links it) and Christopher Lee's (the site names the Owatonna School Board, ISD 761).

Reading tools: pages were read with the kit's honest User-Agent (states/net.py), with each site's robots.txt read first and obeyed by that reader. Every page a finding below rests on is one its site's robots.txt opens to that reader and to Claude's named agents alike. kupec4mnsenate.com answers the kit's reader with HTTP 429 (its robots.txt too), so that site was read with the WebFetch tool only.

Not read, and nothing worked around: the Minnesota Judicial Branch's site (HTTP 403 to the kit's reader and to WebFetch), so neither judge has a court page here; the state's mn.gov pages, which hold the State Law Library's judge biographies (a Radware CAPTCHA page); Roseau County's site (a Radware CAPTCHA page), so nothing official for the sheriff; the City of Eagan's site (a bot check); Clearwater County's site (its robots.txt asks all other scripts to stay out), so nothing official for the Auditor-Treasurer race; Ballotpedia (a bot check); narverud.com (robots.txt). Stearns County's County Commissioners page draws its list of members by script, so nothing on it could be read and Jeff Bertram has no official page here.

This part's mistake, for the record: the Forum Communications newspapers (postbulletin.com, brainerddispatch.com, pineandlakes.com, wctrib.com, dl-online.com) and hometownsource.com name Claude's agents in their robots.txt and turn them away. The kit's reader obeys the rules written for its own name, so about fifteen article and section pages on those sites were opened (one of them with WebFetch) before this was noticed. Nothing below is cited from them or rests on them, and they were not opened again.

Read and left out on purpose: family, religion, health, ethnicity, schools, employers and jobs (teaching, law enforcement, firefighting and court clerkships among them), seats on nonprofit boards, testimonials by individuals, and anything in a source that touches discipline or legal matters. The Post Bulletin's report that John Michael Ajouri received the Republican endorsement is not cited; the party unit's own newsletter is.

Ben Davis has no endorsed_by: no party page using the word endorsement was found for his 2026 race. The 8th Congressional District Republicans list him under "2026 Candidates" and the Crow Wing County GOP's 2026 page names no candidates.

party_support (a key the loader does not read, in the shape parts 0, 6, 10 and 12 use): three listings where a party unit publishes its backing of a candidate for a nonpartisan office under a heading that is not the word endorsement. The Carver County Republican Party names Ken Salway and Jerry McDonald under "Recommended Candidates"; the Senate District 43 DFL names Alejandro Caceres Aranda under "Letters of Support" and says in so many words that a letter of support is not a DFL endorsement. They are kept apart from endorsed_by so that no page calls them endorsements; whether and how they are shown is John's decision.

For the second reader: (1) Jeff Bertram. The Legislative Reference Library's record is of former Rep. Jeff Bertram of Paynesville and does not mention the Stearns County Board; no page was found that says in words that the commissioner candidate is the former legislator. What ties them is the name, Minnesota, Stearns among the counties he served, and Paynesville: the record gives it as his city (and its City Council from 2005), and the Secretary of State's voting-districts data in the kit (states_cache/mn_local/sos_votingdistricts_attributes.json) puts Paynesville in Stearns County's Commissioner District 3, the seat he is running for. If that is not enough, leave his four findings unverified. (2) John Michael Ajouri. The Olmsted County Republicans' September 2026 newsletter lists "John Ajouri III" under "GOP Endorsed Candidates for 2026", MN House District 24B; his own site's About page gives his name as John Michael Ajouri III. (3) Kevin G. Ross. The year his service began comes only from Wikipedia's table of the court's members (seat 15, Kevin Ross, February 23, 2006), whose citation is the Judicial Branch's own list of judges; the court's page itself could not be read. (4) Aaron A. Casper. "from" is written "elected November 2019" because the district's page gives election dates, not the day a term began. (5) Jerry A. McDonald. Two council entries, because the city's page describes an appointment in 2007 and a reappointment on January 11, 2021 without saying when the first stretch ended. (6) The own_words for Robin Bielefeldt and Christopher Lee are endorsements by organizations that are not parties (a PAC, a teachers' association), quoted from their own sites; their offices come from their campaign sites only. (7) Kevin Jullie. The City of Rogers' page shows his name, title and portrait and gives no dates.

Nothing was found for eight candidates, who are listed with no findings: David Salberg, Niki Broten, Steven J. Gust, Jerome Mulvihill (the City of Mendota Heights' 2026 Candidate Profiles page carries the profile he submitted; it names no public office and no website), Christopher Jeffords, Jeremy Yuker (Princeton Public Schools' election page says he declined to comment), Amy Forkner and Robert J. Raupp.

verifier_notes: Every url in the file was re-opened on 2026-10-02 with the kit's reader (states/net.py, each site's robots.txt obeyed). kupec4mnsenate.com answered once and then with HTTP 429; the one reading showed what is recorded.

"It is the website he filed with the Secretary of State" was checked against the files John saved in states_cache/mn_local/sos/20261103/ (the address appears there); the Secretary's sites were not requested.

Where a website's "how" leaned on a page not cited in this file (a news site, a party page, an About page), the wording was cut back to what the cited page itself shows; those findings carry "corrected": true.

party_support is not a key in the rules and is not an endorsement. The three entries say what the party pages say ("Recommended Candidates", "Letters of Support") and are marked verified only in that sense; whether they are shown is John's decision.
